articles.title: Review launched into how pub and hotel business rates calculated
articles.summary: The review of how rates are calculated in England and Wales could lead to reform of the system.
articles.content:
A review is being launched into the way business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels in England and Wales, and could lead to a reform of the system.

The Treasury says business rates expert Jerry Schurder will lead the review into rate valuations and report back in March 2027, with the government calling for the views of landlords, hoteliers and business owners to feed in to the process.

Last month, Andy Burnham announced a 20% cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England, to come into effect in April.

Pub groups have argued they face disproportionately higher rates bills, but other businesses have called for a wider reform of the rates system.

According to the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA), 161 pubs closed in the first three months of this year across England, Scotland and Wales, equating to the loss of around 2,400 jobs.

Rising business rates are cited as one issue facing the sector, although there have also been complaints that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made staff costs more expensive.

James Murray, financial secretary to the Treasury, said the new review would look at "a rethink of valuations - so that we can build a fairer system for the future".

Emma McClarkin, chief executive of the BBPA, said: "For years pubs have paid a disproportionately higher business rates bill which has ground down their ability to keep the doors open, so this review is sorely needed and hugely welcome."

The BBPA says pubs are valued differently for rates than retail venues. Instead of being based just on floor area, they are judged by a measure called Fair Maintainable Trade - which means when a pub's turnover increases, so does its rates bill.

Schurder is a former business rates policy lead at advisory firm Newmark UK, and his review will feed into the next rates revaluation in 2029.

His appointment was welcomed by Craig Beaumont of the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) who said he would bring "crucial heavyweight business rates expertise into the Treasury".

However, Beaumont said the government needed to address the wider business rates system and exempt more smaller firms by increasing the rates relief threshold for small businesses.

Tom Ironside from the British Retail Consortium also welcomed the review but said it was "vitally important that the needs of retailers are not overlooked".

Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the review was "far too late for a sector this Labour government has already done its best to kill off".

"Tax hikes on business premises and jobs, alongside job-destroying regulation in the Employment Rights Act, have left many hospitality businesses on the brink," he said.

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said reform of business rates was "long overdue", but also called for an emergency VAT cut and a reverse to jobs tax changes "which have hammered hospitality in particular".
articles.reasoning: The article reports on a government-initiated review aimed at reforming business rates for pubs and hotels, which could lead to fairer taxation and support for struggling hospitality businesses. This has broad significance for many small businesses and employees in the sector, addressing economic challenges and potentially preserving jobs and community hubs.
articles.personality_title: New review aims to make pub and hotel business rates fairer
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Many pubs and hotels in England and Wales face high business rates, which are taxes based on property value. These costs have made it harder for some businesses to stay open, leading to job losses and closures.

**What happened** – The UK government has started a review to look at how business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels. Jerry Schurder, an expert in business rates, will lead this review and report back by March 2027. The government is asking landlords, hoteliers, and business owners to share their views.

**Impact** – This review could change the way business rates are set, making the system fairer. Pubs have been paying more because their rates are based on a measure called Fair Maintainable Trade, which increases with their sales. Changing this could help pubs stay open and save jobs, as many have closed recently due to high costs.

**What's next step** – The review will help shape the next official business rates check in 2029. The government might also consider raising the amount small businesses can earn before they have to pay rates, helping more small firms.

**One-sentence takeaway** – A government review is underway to create a fairer business rates system for pubs and hotels, aiming to support these important local businesses and their employees.
articles.personality_title_fr: Une nouvelle revue vise à rendre les taxes commerciales des pubs et hôtels plus équitables
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – De nombreux pubs et hôtels en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles paient des taxes commerciales élevées basées sur la valeur de leur propriété. Ces coûts rendent difficile la survie de certaines entreprises, causant des fermetures et des pertes d’emplois.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Le gouvernement britannique a lancé une revue pour examiner comment sont calculées les taxes commerciales pour les pubs et hôtels. Jerry Schurder, expert des taxes commerciales, dirigera cette revue et rendra son rapport en mars 2027. Le gouvernement invite les propriétaires et exploitants à donner leur avis.

**Impact** – Cette revue pourrait modifier la manière dont les taxes sont fixées, pour rendre le système plus juste. Les pubs paient souvent plus car leurs taxes sont basées sur le chiffre d’affaires, ce qui augmente leurs coûts. Changer cela pourrait aider les pubs à rester ouverts et préserver des emplois.

**Prochaine étape** – La revue orientera la prochaine réévaluation officielle des taxes commerciales en 2029. Le gouvernement pourrait aussi augmenter le seuil de revenus avant de payer ces taxes, aidant ainsi plus de petites entreprises.

**Une phrase clé** – Une revue gouvernementale est en cours pour créer un système de taxes commerciales plus juste pour les pubs et hôtels, afin de soutenir ces commerces locaux importants et leurs employés.
articles.personality_title_es: Nueva revisión busca hacer más justos los impuestos comerciales para pubs y hoteles
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Muchos pubs y hoteles en Inglaterra y Gales enfrentan altos impuestos comerciales, que se basan en el valor de la propiedad. Estos costos han dificultado que algunos negocios sigan abiertos, causando cierres y pérdida de empleos.

**Qué pasó** – El gobierno del Reino Unido inició una revisión para analizar cómo se calculan los impuestos comerciales para pubs y hoteles. Jerry Schurder, un experto en impuestos comerciales, liderará esta revisión y entregará un informe en marzo de 2027. El gobierno pide a propietarios y empresarios que compartan sus opiniones.

**Impacto** – Esta revisión podría cambiar la forma en que se establecen los impuestos comerciales, haciendo el sistema más justo. Los pubs han estado pagando más porque sus impuestos se basan en sus ventas, lo que aumenta sus costos. Cambiar esto podría ayudar a que los pubs sigan abiertos y se salven empleos.

**Próximo paso** – La revisión ayudará a preparar la próxima evaluación oficial de impuestos en 2029. También se podría aumentar el límite de ingresos para que más pequeñas empresas estén exentas.

**Una frase clave** – El gobierno está revisando el sistema de impuestos comerciales para pubs y hoteles con el objetivo de apoyar a estos negocios locales y a sus trabajadores.
